off-grid-ai-skills-codebase-audit-a-modu.description: Health check one module or service and recommend what to do with it: leave it, clean it up, refactor it with care, or don't touch it without a senior. Covers what it does, who depends on it, risk, test coverage, churn and rule breaks. Use when the user says "audit this module", "is it safe to refactor X", "how healthy is this service" or "should we rewrite X".

off-grid-ai-skills-codebase-blast-radius.description: Before editing a file or symbol, find everything that depends on it, score how risky the change is, and stop for approval when it's high. Use before changing a shared function, type, API, schema or config, or when the user asks "is it safe to change this", "what breaks if I change X" or "what's the blast radius".

off-grid-ai-skills-testing-bug-trap.description: Write and fix tests that catch real bugs, by testing behaviour, faking only the device boundary and seeding data the way the product writes it. Use when a bug needs a test that fails first, or a unit test is failing or flaky, or when the user says "add a test for this bug", "fix this failing test" or "why is this test flaky". For the bar every test is held to, use test-like-a-user.

off-grid-ai-skills-testing-click-everyth.description: Test your app one module at a time by looking at it like a user does. Your agent lists every route from the router, screenshots every route and state, clicks the buttons, makes the app produce real output and reads it, fixes what doesn't make sense, adds replayable end-to-end tests, and reports. Use when you say "test every page", "/click-everything", "sweep the app", "visually test this module", or when there is no other work queued.

off-grid-ai-skills-review-code-check.description: Hold every change to one engineering standard and get a pass or fail with evidence before it merges. SETUP installs quality gates in a repo, PLAN designs a task against the bar (separation of concerns, SOLID, DRY, tests), AUDIT reviews a diff dimension by dimension. Use when you say "audit this diff", "is this ready to merge", "/code-check", "plan this subsystem", or "set up quality gates". Not for small fixes.

off-grid-ai-skills-codebase-deploy-witho.description: Check everything before and after a production deploy, with a rollback plan and clear rollback triggers. Use when the user is about to deploy or just deployed, or says "is it safe to deploy", "pre-deploy check", "post-deploy check" or "we're going to prod". Not for committing, opening PRs or app store releases.

off-grid-ai-skills-testing-dont-break-it.description: Your agent changes code in small, additive, checked commits that never skip hooks and never block on long jobs. Use before editing code, running checks, committing or pushing in any repo, or when you say "change code safely", "commit this properly", "small commits" or "follow the engineering rules".

off-grid-ai-skills-testing-fix-it-for-re.description: Fix bugs at the system level instead of patching symptoms, by reproducing each bug with a failing probe, finding who already solved the general problem, and committing small checked changes safely even when several agents share one checkout. Use when fixing a bug, especially one that came back, or when the user says "no hack fixes", "fix it properly", "this keeps breaking", "fix the root cause" or "fix-it-for-real".

off-grid-ai-skills-codebase-learn-this-c.description: Get to know an unfamiliar codebase fast. Maps what it does, its modules, entry points, riskiest files, recent changes and the rules not to break, writes it to CODEBASE.md, then answers questions from that map with sources. Use when the user is new to a project or says "onboard me", "where do I start", "how does X work here", "where is the payment logic" or "give me an overview".

off-grid-ai-skills-review-never-twice.description: Turn each pull request review into a sharper engineering standard, so the same mistake doesn't come back. Your agent keeps only the general lessons from a review, writes each into code-check with a signal a grep can catch, and logs its source. Use when you say "learn from this review", "/never-twice", "update the standard from these comments", or at the end of safe-to-merge.

off-grid-ai-skills-codebase-plan-from-sc.description: Plan a new project before any code exists. Researches the domain, then has an architect, a product lead and a security lead plan it independently, and merges them into one PLAN.md that names where they disagree. Use when the user is starting something new and says "plan this", "help me start this project", "write a PLAN.md" or "what should the stack be". Not for changes to an existing codebase (use learn-this-codebase first).

off-grid-ai-skills-review-safe-to-merge.description: Take a pull request from "the diff exists" to "ready to merge" and keep it there. Your agent audits its diff, gathers every review signal, answers each comment, fixes behind the checks and re-reviews until nothing blocks. Use when you say "review this PR", "get this PR merge-ready", "/safe-to-merge", "address the review comments", or after pushing to a PR with open comments.

off-grid-ai-skills-codebase-stay-in-the-.description: Check that code follows the project's architecture rules, such as which modules may import which, no cycles, and services talking only through their APIs. Reports each new violation with the commit that added it and a fix. Use on a PR that crosses module boundaries, when the user asks "are we following the architecture" or "is this import allowed", or as a weekly health check.

off-grid-ai-skills-testing-test-like-a-u.description: Hold every test to one bar, real integration tests that walk the whole user journey and prove the intended end state, with fakes only at boundaries you can't control. Use when writing, fixing, reviewing or auditing tests, or when the user says "write a test", "add tests for this", "are these tests any good", "test this properly", "audit the tests" or "review this test".

off-grid-ai-skills-codebase-tests-for-ol.description: Add end-to-end tests to code that has none, in tiers by confidence, and run every test before handing it over. Use before refactoring untested code, after inheriting a project, or when the user says "add tests for this flow", "write e2e tests for login" or "we have no tests for X".
